body: Recent work on large audio-language models (LALMs) explores adaptive reasoning to balance accuracy and efficiency. However, existing approaches often rely on coarse-grained difficulty estimation, overlooking the diverse factors that determine reasoning effort. We address this limitation by deriving five-dimensional difficulty scores and compressed reasoning traces from complementary offline assessments. Based on this characterization, we propose SWEAR, a difficulty-aware reasoning framework that learns difficulty signals during supervised fine-tuning and uses reinforcement learning to adapt reasoning allocation across reasoning stages. Experiments on MMAU-test-mini and MMAR show that SWEAR improves accuracy while substantially reducing generated tokens, shortening reasoning for easy instances without sacrificing performance on difficult ones.
summaryZh: 该研究提出了SWEAR（Section-Wise Efficient Audio Reasoning via Self-Rated Difficulty）框架，用于解决大型音频语言模型（LALM）在推理效率和准确性之间的权衡问题。SWEAR通过从离线评估中提取五维难度分数和压缩推理轨迹，实现了难度感知的自适应推理。该框架在训练过程中学习难度信号，并利用强化学习来动态调整跨推理阶段的资源分配。在MMAR等基准测试上的实验表明，SWEAR在提高准确性的同时显著减少了生成token数量，有效缩短了简单实例的推理时间，而不会牺牲对困难实例的性能。
